purpose: Characterize the existing migration fixture before a native document adapter can claim legacy compatibility. This is not byte-for-byte source-to-export equality and not installed-surface acceptance.

forbidden: Use numeric layer index as a persistent reference
Renumber an existing layerUid or strokeId
Treat documentId as a persisted project UUID
Infer a cross-frame shape identity from an ordinary strokeId

migrationFacts.meaning: A matte without an explicit source UID binds to the layer directly above.
A fill without hasRealStroke retains the historical white fallback.

roundtrip.firstPass: Import the v12 fixture through the characterized legacy adapter and export a canonical v13 project.
roundtrip.secondPass: Open that v13 canonical export in a fresh document context, then export again.
roundtrip.expected: The first and second canonical exports match except for the known workspace panel-order drift below; preserved IDs and every other serialized value remain unchanged.

knownBaselineDrift.change: canvas-sec and combine-opts-sec move from after shapes-sec to the front, in that order
knownBaselineDrift.scope: exact observed baseline only; not a waiver for arbitrary workspace or unknown-field loss
knownBaselineDrift.beforeAfterArrays: not_asserted: the checked migration fixture, expected.json, and reference fixture checks do not encode exact panelOrder arrays; do not invent them

nativeTransitionRequirements.documentIdentity: A fresh open creates a runtime documentId distinct from file path and stored values; a replacement rotates it and invalidates old requests/jobs.
nativeTransitionRequirements.contentRevision: Migration/import completion creates an owner-assigned contentRevision; reopening may create a new documentId even when project content is equal.
nativeTransitionRequirements.contextIdentity: The selected scene/component/montage contextId is carried into evaluation and must not change persisted layer/stroke identities.

nonEvidence: No native engine implementation was run by this oracle.
No browser, installed desktop, renderer, or export acceptance is claimed.
A pure parser result alone is insufficient; the applicable save/import/export path must be exercised by a future acceptance packet.
